name: קַלָּי
gloss: swift; or light (not explained in scripture)
summary: Kallai, head of the priestly house of Sallai in the days of Joiakim the high priest, after the return from Babylon; named only in Neh 12:20. The name is formed from קַל “swift, light” with the ending ‑ai, as many names of that period are; scripture does not explain it, so “swift” rests on the adjective's use (2Sa 2:18).

evidence.note: “לְסַלַּי קַלָּי”: of Sallai, Kallai, among the heads of the priests' fathers' houses (Neh 12:12).
The word the name is formed from: Asahel was “קַל בְּרַגְלָיו”, light of foot.

note: Only one bearer. The derivation from קַל is the plain reading of the consonants; the ‑ai ending is read as a short form (hypocoristic) as in other post-exilic names, which is not shown from scripture.
